Uniform Title: Bhāvacūḍāmaṇi Author: Vidyākaṇṭha Manuscript: NGMCP 6/1748, Reel Number A 989/23
Notes: Revision 0: December 16, 2013 Publication Country: India p. 1a)
Salutations to the venerable Guru Gaṇapati.

Although various kinds of means for accomplishment have been written down, nevertheless, mantras do not succeed without the proper disposition (bhāva); therefore, the *Bhāvacūḍāmaṇi* is now being written.
In that *Cūḍāmaṇi* [Tantra]:
The illustrious Bhairava said:
O Mother, O Goddess, O Mahāmāyā, who brings about both bondage and liberation!
Now I desire to hear the most excellent mantra of the lineage of gurus.
The Goddess said:
The lineage of the gurus is indeed manifold; due to the weight of the extensive details of the mantras and because time itself is beginningless, how could I possibly describe it?
Having failed to know the teacher's family, one will become lost on the path;
for one who is lost on the path, great knowledge does not come within the range of its proper fruit.
If there is no lineage succession for the gurus who have become disciples, then the tantras, mantras, and vidyās are fruitless; of this there is no doubt.
Whether it be twenty, nine, seven, or even three generations of the lineage of gurus— if one does not know them, the disciple shall have his lineage destroyed.
O Maheśvara, one should know that the lineage of the Guru is more important than one's own lineage; O Lord, one should know that the mantra is more important than the father.
Therefore, O Lord of Gods, listen briefly to these teachers in all cases:
first of all, O Lord of Gods, the giver of the mantra is the supreme teacher in every instance.
You are indeed the supreme and subordinate guru, while I am the Parameṣṭhin;
thus, in all the tantras, the Vidyās are of self-manifested form.
From that [source], the lineage of my own gurus arose in human form;
by that very [lineage], I, the portions of the state [of liberation], and especially my devotees [are sustained].
He is the source of all desired mantras and the bestower of auspiciousness everywhere;
Śiva and those Brahmins devoted to Śiva are also guides in every place.
Gaṇeśa and the Gāṇapatyas consider him the master of the Gaṇa-initiation;
likewise, O child, Sūrya and the Sauras [consider him so], as does Viṣṇu, who is devoted to Viṣṇu.
O God, I shall briefly describe before you the divine lineage gurus, as well as the siddha lineage gurus and the human lineage gurus.
In all tantras and mantras, a fourfold mantra system is proclaimed;
therein, Kālikā Devī comes first—listen now to her lineage of gurus.
Mahādevī, Mahākāla, Tripura, and Bhairava are declared to be the Gurus of the Divine Current (divyaugha); now I shall describe the Gurus of the Siddha Current (siddhaugha).
Brahmānanda, Pūrṇadeva, Calavitta, Calācala, Kumāra, Krodhana, Varada, and Smaradīpana.
Listen, my dear, to the multitudes of men: Māyā and Māyāvatī, Vimanas, Kṛpaṇa, Bhīmasena, and Sudhākara.
Mīna, Gorakṣaka, Bhojadeva,
Prajāpati, Mūladeva, Āruntideva, Vighneśvara, and Hutāśana.
Somapānanda and Sahaja are remembered as the gurus of Kālikā.
Now I shall describe the gurus of Tārā, who bestow both seen and unseen fruits.
With hair standing erect, with sky-like hair, blue-throated, and bull-bannered—
these are the divine streams that bestow success; listen, my child, with an attentive mind.
Vasiṣṭha, Kūrmanātha, Nīlanātha, Maheśvara,
and Harinātha— now I shall speak of the lineages of human gurus.
Tārāvatī, Bhānumatī, Jayā, Vidyā, Mahodarī;
Mukhānanda, Parānanda, Pārijāta, and Kuleśvara.
O Supreme Lord, Virūpākṣa and Bhairavī have been described; thus has the Kula of Tāriṇī been told within the Siddha-ogha, the Mānava-ogha, and the Divya-ogha.
Akṣobhya, who bears the form of a nāga and possesses three forms, is situated upon the crown of all;
now, O beloved, I shall describe Svapnāvatī to you among the goddesses.
Parānanda, Pūrṇeśa, Janārdana the God of gods,
Pūrṇeśī, Sundarī, Mohinī, Rati, and Kāmikā.
Pulastya, endowed with being, is the performer of the rite for attracting heroes;
the host of Siddhas is present, as is the virtuous goddess and the moon-crested Bhairava.
In the multitude of men, there was the goddess Kalāvatī, full of patience;
and among the gods, Maheśa named Viṣṇu, who was Gaṅgeśa, the lord of those who remember him.
Kalānanda, Kumārī, and all refined women—
those who are clever among all castes and those who have reached every stage of life.
Whether she be a young girl or intoxicated by youth, or whether she be without a husband or have sons—
if the practitioner, having abandoned the status of a guru toward women, [acts thus].
Whether by speech, mind, or even body, one who acts like a dreamer shall be defeated;
he, being possessed of every fault, is a defiler of his lineage and must be abandoned.
Therefore, with every effort, one should avoid doing what is displeasing even to one's own wife,
let alone to the wives of others, for they are all portions of My own self.
Now, my child, I shall explain to you the lineage of gurus of the sixteen [initiations]:
Ānandanātha and Deva, as well as Paraprakāśaka.
Beyond that is the god Paraśiva, and beyond that is Paraśakti;
then Kauleśvara, Śaktideva, Akuleśāna, and Kāmuka.
O Bhairava, I shall describe the pure lineages and those worn out by worldly enjoyment; O God, this is the convention regarding the innate [lineages]. O dear one, now hear about the human lineages.
Gagana, Viṣṇu, Vimala, Sahaja,
Bhuvana, Nīla, Svādu, and Priya— these are said to be the most excellent of gurus.
The illustrious Bhairava said:
The fourfold knowledge has been declared by Durgā as being equal to herself;
setting that aside, how can Tārā—who is said to be most difficult to attain—be described?
The illustrious Bhairava said:
"Well asked by you, my child, that which brings happiness to all living beings!
Although there is no cause for wonder, Durgā is just as Tārā is."
Nevertheless, fear arose at every step regarding its manifestation;
listen, my child, [to the names of] Mahādeva, the Gurus, Durgā, and those born of Manu.
The Supreme Self, supreme bliss, the one seated in the highest, the source of splendor;
Kṛṣṇa, Time, the Lord of the arts (or digits), and the divine hosts beginning with Bhairava.
Nārada, Kaśyapa, Śambhu, Bhārgava, and Kulakaulika—
these are proclaimed as the five great Siddha lineages of the Mahādevas.
Rudrācārya, Kṣamācārya, the one known as Pavanāśana,
Kumārīśa, Śaktidhara, Ghanānanda, and Prakāśaka.
Hariśarman, Viṣṇuśarman, Dattātreya, Priyaṃvada,
the goddess Bahulā Śākinī, and Caryānātha are proclaimed [as the lineage].
Lopāmudrā will speak of the gurus; listen, O Bhairava, as it arises in this context.
First is the divine Supreme Lord (Parameśvara), and after that, the Supreme Goddess (Parameśī).
Mitrīśa, Sajjīśa, and Uḍḍīśa are divine practitioners;
Caryānātha, Lopāmudrā, Agastya, and Kāladīpana [are likewise].
Then I shall describe the multitudes of Mānavas, and after that, the Teachers of Dharma (Dharmācāryas):
the Lord Muktakeśīśvara and likewise Dīpakanātha.
Viṣṇu, Prabhākara, and after him Manojña;
then Kalyāṇadeva, Ratnadeva, Śrīrāmānanda, and Devaka.
The gurus whose names end with the word Ānandanātha bestow all supernatural powers;
alternatively, in all the scriptures, the gurus are indicated by [the suffix] *sarva*.
O Lord Maheśvara, listen, O God, to the Kulacūḍāmaṇi:
in whichever mantras those various groups of sages (ṛṣigaṇa) are traditionally remembered.
Each of those is worthy of worship; he is to be worshipped first. I have spoken this in brief: out of ignorance, one should indeed worship the triad of gurus by their names.
Either four or seven [prostrations] should be performed, but not more than that;
then [one should prostrate to] the gurus, the paramagurus, and then the parāparagurus.
The Parameṣṭhin and the Gurus have likewise been declared as gurus;
O child, if one should perform worship without first worshipping the gurus, [the rite is fruitless].
O child, for the pacification of that fault, one should perform the family worship (kulapūjā);
whatever merit may be gained there is tripled through the performance of the family worship.
How could there be the inspection of the lineage, or the sprinkling and wiping?
Where is the offering of flowers, where is purification, and where is the cleansing through ritual placement?
O Vaṭukeśvara, if one is initiated and belongs to a noble family, or if the family [is noble],
one should bring the Guru into that body and perform remembrance at your feet.
O Maheśvara, I do not know my guru’s name nor his lineage;
by the grace of the dust of your lotus feet, grant me the state of servitude.
Having thus praised one's own lineage and guru with this hymn,
O child, if one worships by means of that [guru's] name, thereby the worship of the guru is accomplished.
In the worship of Svapnāvatī, one should meditate upon the Guru in the form of the Kula;
for in that context, the Kula is as the Guru, and not so the Kula-practitioner.
The lineage succession has been told; without knowing it, the lotus of the family [should not be revealed].
It must not be given anywhere to anyone, even to one who acts as a mere kisser.
O Lord of the Kula, the name of these animals should be taken with the word "Agni" [at the beginning];
whether in the Vaiṣṇava, Śākta, or Gāṇapatya Tantra.
Then, having meditated upon one's own guru and worshipped the four gurus,
one should chant the mantra to the deity and should not practice any restriction.
The illustrious Bhairava said:
O Great Goddess, please out of compassion explain the conduct of the pledge (samayācāra), the secret signs (saṃketa), and likewise the symbolic states (bhāvasaṃketaka) as they have been indicated.
Among all mantras and vidyās, as well as the conventions of their inner nature,
it is likewise the Śaktitantras that especially bestow all accomplishments.
The Goddess said:
O God, the nature [of the path] is threefold, namely divine, heroic, and animal, in sequence;
likewise, the gurus here are of three kinds, as are the mantras and deities.
O Mahādeva, the first state is the most excellent, bestowing all prosperity;
the second is middling, and the third is censured by all.
O God, through extensive practices such as much recitation, security, and physical austerities, mantras do not yield fruit in that tantra without devotion.
O Hero, what is the use of ritual means (sādhana), O Lord, or what use are the various lineages of practitioners?
What indeed is the use of worshipping the sacred seats (pīṭha), or of feeding virgins and so forth?
What is the use of giving pleasure to one’s own wife, and likewise what is the use of others?
What is the use of the state of having conquered the senses, and what is the use of performing ritual conduct?
If one whose self is purified by devotion were not devoted to the Divine,
one would not attain liberation through devotion, nor would one increase one's lineage through devotion.
Through meditative absorption (bhāva), there shall be the increase of the lineage; through meditative absorption, there is the purification of the body.
What is the use of elaborate ritual placements (nyāsa)? What is the use of elaborate purifications of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi)?
If, despite such worship, no spiritual disposition arises,
by whom then is the Vidyā not worshipped, and by whom is it not worshipped?
O Lord of Gods, the absence of fruit arises from the non-existence of existence;
my mind is apprehensive regarding the disclosure of this secret.
O Lord, since one who is envious of the three worlds generally encounters such people everywhere,
how can I describe that to you when I do not see anyone else in this desolate place?
The illustrious Bhairava said:
"O Goddess, by your grace, I have obtained this Vidyā that dispels dreams;
it is the foremost initiation for those who have taken refuge in all Māyās, and it is the most skillful among the capable."
"O Goddess, there exists a cause for the sleep of all beings;
I shall explain it, provided that you do not harbor ill-will toward me, as if I were your son."
The Goddess said:
First, the divine state is described; listen with reverence to where the deity resides and how that splendor is joined with a mass of light.
Having visualized the entire world as consisting of light and fashioned into a form,
[one should worship] with mantras corresponding to each respective form, whether by their own specific mantras or otherwise.
Having seen oneself as composed of that [essence], and likewise all states of being,
one should meditate with a restrained mind, contemplating all of that within the woman.
She is endowed with the excellence of all families, born from various luminaries,
or even originating from various lands, and is possessed of virtue and loveliness.
From the second year onwards until she reaches her tenth year, she should be known as a *kumārī*; in that state, she bestows the fruit of the mantra.
O Deva, by worshipping a maiden and also by feeding a maiden—
one, two, three, or more— there is no doubt that she bestows the fruit of the seeds [of merit].
Having given flowers, fruit, or likewise betel nut, betel leaf,
and whatever substance is dear to the child, the worshipper should bow down.
Having meditated upon himself within her limbs as one whose behavior was that of a child,
he engaged with them in pleasant conversation, play, curiosity, and the like.
By performing whatever is pleasing to him in whatever manner, one shall become a Siddheśvara;
therefore, it will be declared that [the number of repetitions] extends up to sixteen.
In that regard, if it is the manifestation of existence, that existence is considered supreme;
having drunk [it] from the feet up to the crest-lock, one should drink it again and again.
May the darkness be shattered by the moonlight of her nails and face; may it be reduced to the form of a skull-fragment by the splendor of the breasts of that beautiful woman.
The hero should always possess a gentle inner disposition and remain free from agitation; his knees, shanks, thighs, and hips should be well-rounded and beautiful.
With her navel and the line of body hair, with her chest and full breasts,
with her neck, the corners of her eyes, the tips of her hair, and her exquisite smiles;
As long as he remains with his senses moistened by the overflowing intoxication of honey, playful in his natural disposition, and contented, he becomes the refuge of the fourfold aims of life.
Furthermore, at the time of cessation, her own pair of breasts below that [navel] takes on a form like a drop on the face, filled with the nectar of existence.
O God, it is the immortalization of all knowledge, complete, the bestower of the power of all speech,
the accomplisher of all aims, and the provider of all protection.
Having thoroughly prepared that mandala below it, extending even to the limit of the supreme aeon (parārddha),
which contains all beings beginning with the gods and is saluted by all the gods;
O God, it brings complete joy to all, provides protection for all,
accomplishes all aims, and sets in motion the subjugation of all.
This meditation on Kāmakalā is to be kept strictly secret by the most excellent practitioners;
having meditated upon it, or having merely remembered or seen it, one becomes endowed with Kāmakalā through that meditation.
Through the contemplation of the reality of the moments (kṣaṇatattva), the accumulation of states arises;
and having thoroughly contemplated that entire form of their creative power within the [spiritual] lineages.
Since one is born into a noble family, how is that explained?
Because in that family, one personally contemplates reality according to its true nature.
Therefore, one who knows the scriptures of your lineage should be honored with great effort—
whether it be the family deity or the personal deity— whoever possesses unwavering faith in them.
That man alone is blessed in the world and possesses true discernment, in whose family the lineage-initiation (kuladīkṣā) exists; for he alone indeed destroys the sins of that [lineage].
If one who has not been initiated should go to a *kulāṣaṃpa*, a loss of spiritual accomplishment (*siddhi*) arises.
p.
6a) O Lord, how should one born of a noble family worship the Supreme Goddess? For she exists in the form of the scriptures, yet [her] form is... [illegible].
The supreme accomplishment is that which makes known what is to be known and increases joy.
Therefore, having risen and grasped them by the tips of their hands, one should serve them as one's own self.
Having meditated there upon Kāmakalā, who is seated on the left side, who possesses her own color, who can assume any form at will, and whose complete body consists of the bindu and other elements;
Having first arranged the placement of the hair, the forehead mark (tilaka), the necklace, the armlets, the lac-dye, and all the ornaments, one should employ the ritual substances (kuladravya).

What is the reason for the assembly of the virtuous? Having given and having eaten, the practitioner should not ask about the lineage; within that [inquiry], what is there of the mundane or the supramundane?
The five flowers arising from the [five] elements are not prescribed in the Kula traditions and the like;
one who knows the Kula but lacks the *kalā* will certainly perish, even if he is an accomplished adept (*siddha*).

Having perceived defects and so forth therein, one should not cultivate affection through distorted training; for if one employs harsh methods toward that which is already distorted, it will be fruitless.
O Lord, since the secret of the Kula scripture is the very root of the Kula,
it is better to abandon the Kula than even the Kula-guru.
O dear one, one's own family is not fit to be abandoned even because of observed faults;
standing upon this tree of my lineage, I shall nourish my own kin.
Therefore, with every effort, one must protect it diligently;
for even if, by the conjunction of fortune, there should be an abundance of noble lineages within a good family.
Every form must be established; one should abandon all contrariety.
There is a separate location, a separate meditation, a separate worship, and a separate praise.
This must be performed with effort; what is the use of these many words?
O Lord of Gods, may I remain in my family—there should be no hesitation in this matter.
Through the practice of placing trust in them, the presiding deity of that region perishes;
by means of joy, there is a bath in nectar for me—of this there is no doubt.
Born of noble lineage, I roar amidst the great battle, striking down the heroes;
I do not act out of ignorance here, for I protect the world with constancy.
Garrulousness, hatred toward my husband, harsh speech, quarreling, and so forth, as well as wandering about and the like— because of these, I am not even slightly dear to you.
Through the shattering of the vessel of the universe, he becomes endowed with that perfection within the individual soul;
without the Kula, my perfection is not attained anywhere.
The illustrious Bhairava said:
O Goddess, how is it that you always grant liberation to this four-cornered [world]?
Since the nature of the Kula has been awakened, fulfill my doubt.
The illustrious Goddess said:
The path to liberation is indeed manifold;
[yet] I am pleased solely by means of Kula-yoga—of this there is no doubt.
O King, among the four stages of life, the stage of the Avadhūta is the greatest;
there, through the yoga of my lineage, I am pleased as the bestower of liberation.
If it were not so, listen to that which I shall tell you:
once the state of gnosis has arisen, one should pray to one's own Kaulikī.
Therefore, I shall lead them; by worshipping them in another family, liberation will be attained.
Then, one should practice yoga in the aperture of the Kuṇḍalinī power.
Free from dualities, free from egoism, with his network of channels purified,
the observer of vows sits upon a soft seat, intent on the restraint of the vital breath.
O Śiva, on the outer sides of the spinal column (merudaṇḍa) are the channels consisting of the Moon and the Sun;
in the middle is the Suṣumnā, and in its center is that which has a variegated form.
By that very [thread], the lotus and the five paths beginning with the root are strung together;
Kālikā, in the form of Time, is suspended by the Ḍākinīs and others.
Having reached the root-gate, she, in the form of a serpent, stands there;
then, joined with the piercing wind, she causes even that which is firm to dissolve.
Is this the perpetual radiance of the *śikhā* (topknot) of Kāma, blazing with his breath?
Facing every direction, it has awakened the individual soul (*jīvātman*) within the Supreme.
By practicing that yoga, one attains indeed the supreme immortality;
having forcefully burst through to the end of the nose, one reaches both the moon and the sun.
Having embraced the great lotus of the *ādhāra-cakra* by means of the *suṣumṇā*,
she has reached the middle of the upturned nose, united with the variegated body.
Having pierced upward through that very *liṅga*, one reaches the other *puṣkara*; there,
the witness (*sākṣiṇī*), who bestows liberation, carries away the jewels without being desired.
Restrained by the unseen force (adṛṣṭa), that [individual soul] remains in the proximity of the Supreme;
when it discerns this distinction, it pierces through and goes to the supreme state.
This invisible element, the *jīva*, goes outside day after day;
by the measure of a finger-breadth (*śāṅguli*) each day, it extends half of that [distance] during the night.
It should be double during the time of joy, triple outside of the meal-time;
O Bhairava, if it is after midday, it should be for one day, and if it is outside [the village], for three days.
Or if it is deficient, O Vaṭukeśvara, the vital breath abandons the body from below;
having brought the body to a state of equilibrium, or [if it is] deficient, O Lord of Vaṭuka.
Having filled [the body] and restrained the downward-moving wind at the opening of the Kuṇḍalinī,
one should then lead the individual soul (jīva) to the end of the Nāda.
Having performed the coming and going, the practitioner becomes perfected;
for whatever is drunk or eaten, all that is in the mouth of Kuṇḍalinī.
Having offered oblations, one attains perfection and is no longer bound by worldly existence;
furthermore, for the sake of Kuṇḍalinī, the four elements must be pierced.
O Hemātarddhi, grant me alms; I, the wearer of earrings, am satiating myself while abiding in the state of the Avadhūta, intent upon the bliss of Bhairava.
I am Bhairava, and there is no other than I; there is no deity higher than me anywhere.
There is no mantra superior to that, and nothing has been born that is not composed of me, nor otherwise.
"I am Śiva, I am Bhairava; I am the Sound (Nāda), I am the Mantra, the Leader of the Kula.
Anointed with red sandalwood and adorned with a single loincloth."
Wearing red garlands and garments, he should be endowed with the [proper] cause;
thus, the mendicant monk, intent upon the practice of Bhairava, should go for alms.
He is neither stained by sin nor slain by any creature;
wherever he goes, O Lord of the Earth, this is the instruction regarding his state of enmity.
O Lord, those who are intent on censuring him perish in an instant;
therefore, he should be honored and never treated with contempt.
O Lord of the Gods, for one who possesses desire, there exists that effect which is pleasant or unpleasant;
other than that, O Lord of the Gods, is the detailed practice of dissolution.
The Great Goddess worships the limbs of the Kula family by the mere sight of them,
wherever flowers, incense, betel, and food offerings may be present.
O Kuleśvara, having mentally cast that out through the family-water (kulavāri) from the exterior,
and having united it with the self, one attains the form of the Goddess.
There is no worship, no offering, no ritual placement (nyāsa), no steadfastness, and no vows or the like;
I am the Full, I am Bhairava, I am eternal bliss, and I am the imperishable.
I am of an untainted nature; I am the Lord, free from all forms.
I am endowed with all the scriptures and have reached the further shore of the meaning of all mantras.
There is no deity higher than the Self; none has been born, nor will ever be born.
Having become one whose very form is bliss, he acts for the welfare of all.

O beloved, one should discard fish and other offerings that emit a foul odor; instead, one should partake of meat and other foods combined with various fragrant substances as a divine offering (*divyabali*).
A bath should be performed with fragrant, pure oils and various aromatic substances applied to the body; then, one should have him dressed in very fine and beautiful garments.
With fragrant flower garlands and ornaments of pearl,
his body was smooth, exceedingly sweet, capable of assuming any form at will, and captivating to the mind.
Having made his body auspicious and being intent on gentle speech,
he should maintain a lineage of conversation while contemplating the form of his family.
Day and night, he should dwell intent upon joy,
having brought together women born of all eight castes.
O Maheśvara, O Deva, one should assign names according to the sequence of the scents;
that which is the first Śakti is the twice-born woman whose inner organ is pure.
Though pure, that goddess Svapnāvatī has limbs intoxicated by passion; she possesses divine fragrance and is enchanting. One should apply her mantra there.
Having worshipped with pure flowers and food offerings mixed with salt and honey, one should accomplish one's own practice as previously described.
She who is black, with a dark-blue luster, and honey-golden eyes,
whose pair of breasts are the hearts of practitioners, and who is eternally fragrant.
When Kālī has united with her, she is proclaimed as that very Kālī;
one should worship that Kālī there with flowers and sacrificial offerings.
She who is fair-limbed like a third [moon], with beautiful fragrant eyes—
she is the goddess named Tripurā; one should worship her with red flowers.
That woman who possesses the scent of ichor, her eyes languid from the swaying of intoxication,
having been released by the smell of flesh, is the crusher of the demon Mahiṣāsura.
That woman who has the scent of liquor, red eyes, and is stout-bodied is declared to be Ugratārā; she destroys the sins of her husband.
A woman who possesses aśvagandhā, who has long shanks and is captivating, whose eyes are tremulous with wonder, and who is mounted upon a horse, shall be a bestower of boons.
She who has the stench of raw flesh in her mouth and the smell of rot in her joints,
with hair as dark as blue *varvara* grass— know her to be Durgā, intensely eager for the Great Festival.
Endowed with all the auspicious marks, possessed of various fragrances,
she has beautiful teeth, lovely hair, long eyes, and is enchanting.
Skilled in various amorous graces, she deliberated upon the family scriptures;
her waist was pressed against the chest of her guru, appearing without any intervening space.
She who has beautiful teeth shall be Gaurī, the promoter of all undertakings;
she may be accompanied by various attendants or those of a single kind.
Endowed with color and fragrance, they are proclaimed by name;
they must be protected with great effort so that they remain uninjured.
Having himself become one devoted to desire under the name Kāmeśvara, and having brought about an increase in passion, he should practice the root yoga.
If the *mūla-yoga* occurs there, death shall happen within seven days.
Neither Viṣṇu, nor Hari, nor Śambhu, nor the Goddess, nor the Ṣoḍaśī;
neither even Mṛtyuñjaya, nor Nyāsa, nor Bhāvanā.
O God, for such a person death and decay do not prevail, nor do the deities;
that woman [is freed] by means of the Root Yoga or by the ritual of the Nāgadaṃṣṭrā.
If the embryo is pierced by a thunderbolt or even due to a great disease, O Mahādeva, he dies from that sin; this is most certain.
The duties of the gods are manifold, distinguished by the categories of the seen and the unseen;
O Lord of Gods, they are especially so regarding weapons—what more need be said?
Having concealed her true self through illusion and assuming the form of her own wife, she comes and constantly takes pleasure with him; thus, he is surely destroyed.
Therefore, one who desires spiritual perfection should never perform that [rite] in one's own country;
rather, one should strive toward the Lord of the Gods for the sake of destroying desire.
Having taken up the staff of ritual action (karmadaṇḍa) and having established equality with Śiva,
that vessel was wrapped seven times with the thread of the wheel (cakrasūtra).
O Self-Existent One, you have made yourself a noose for the protection of all beings;
O highly fortunate one, you have been conquered—let the fierce binding be performed!
Having thus consecrated that thread by wrapping it seven times around the limb of Śiva,
and having brought those who are awake to a state of sleep, one should then recite the mantra for inducing slumber.
The two *praṇavas* encased by the *saṃhāra* and *svapnodhinī* [mudrās] are known as the *svapna-mantra*; it causes all living beings to fall asleep.
Having done this, O Lord of Yoga, if one's own family should consist of Maheśa and the others, and if one is devoted to constant remembrance [of them].
Therefore, the wise should occasionally exercise such consideration and perform their duties;
O Varāṅga, listen to my words and hear that which is the cause of auspiciousness.
"Having accomplished this task, you must perform what is required for your own [attainment]. Having been addressed thus, the best of practitioners performed their own respective duties.
Maheśvara declared that the Kula-yoga must not be spoken of nor practiced by the wives of heroes,
the daughters of heroes, or the excellent women who are the offspring of heroes.
One should not rejoice with the practitioners until my own abiding presence occurs;
for when the agitation of the mind has arisen therein, what fruit is there through the root-yoga?
O God, that fruit arises; it is the truth, the truth, and not otherwise.
For the wife of a hero is herself the supreme Maheśvarī.
The primordial and ancient Vidyā, the mother of that lineage, is known as such;
her daughter-in-law is Bhuvaneśānī, the awakener of all mantras.
Whether by right means or by wrong means, if the wife of a hero is a guru,
the practitioner shall accomplish every goal merely by looking at her.
O Lord, if by the power of destiny one obtains a wife who is the consort of a hero,
what successes on this earth would not be achieved after bringing that fruit to maturity?
O Mahādeva, I shall describe the method for the ripening of fruits, which is honored by all the gods; it must not be disclosed under any circumstances.
O Lord, the visible and invisible families—the gods, gandharvas, and kiṃnaras—come for the sake of the ripening of the fruit; therefore, one should reflect with diligent effort.
The dismissal should be performed, as well as the concealment and the pacification of the inner disposition;
by means of the performance of those respective rites, one should make the lineage well-trained.
O Mother, there is no dharma superior to devotion to one's husband in the three worlds;
for a husband is eternally the supreme goal of life, and the husband alone is the ultimate refuge.
The husband alone is the supreme Brahman; the husband is the lord who is dearer than life;
the husband is the master who embodies all sacred fords; the husband is equal to all the gods.
The husband alone is the great guru among all the gods;
even if he arrives, she should approach his side and remain there gazing at his face.
Skilled in discerning facial expressions and gestures, she should look toward her husband’s face; she should provide answers with superior eloquence and withdraw from distant affairs.
That woman who, having abandoned one who embodies all the gods, goes to another man,
will certainly be reborn as a sow, a donkey, a crow, or a jackal.
But I, O Queen, bow down like a son; there is no other affection for me than that.
For he who goes along with you anywhere, assuming the form of a husband, [is truly my father].
O Goddess, while reciting the root mantra, this [substance] should be applied to her body;
if she does not come out by that means, then her own husband himself [should be used].
Furthermore, O disciple, whatever training must be undertaken by a woman of noble family,
she should protect herself according to the prescribed rules as previously stated, and not by her own will alone.

One should perform the great worship of the Yoginīs and the Bhairava of the Vaṭukas for the sake of destroying obstacles, in accordance with the conjunction of the Kula-day, the lunar mansion, and the yoga.
Having written the Kāmikā Root-Vidyā at the root of the primary tree at various times, one is thereafter no longer smeared by obstacles.
O Lord, if one desires the falling of the fruit during the rite of dismissal (visarjana), one should employ the mantra for a duration of time starting from the base of the Vīrapatnī.
O best of the lineage, wherever there is delight for the family of Retas,
there Bhairava, Vaṭuka, and the others assume a physical form corresponding to that [delight].
O Lord, having performed the dedication of the hero therein, they bring about the characteristic of the fruit;
for, O God, having understood the arising of the fruit through signs, statements, and words.
O Lord, having understood from the scripture of knowledge of reality that [the being] is born as a god or born as a human,
one should know the distribution of fruits starting from the fifth [birth] onwards.
Or, from the seventh or eighth month, having placed the hand upon a tree or in the middle of a lake by means of the sandals through the yoga of the withdrawal of the vidyā;
One should indeed recite it eight thousand times; then, by one's own volition, the Lord of the World will fall [upon the target]. When this is done, whatever falls is the fruit ordained by the gods.
And [the vessel] falls down ownerless due to the reversal of the coming and going;
having recognized this sign and its fruit, one should then bring it and wash it in the temple.
Having abandoned the portion consisting of defects and having bowed to the fruit-bearing tree,
one should perform the ripening of the fruit in a copper vessel within the great forest.
Having performed the protection rites and so forth, the wise one, knowing the food to be prepared, should offer it while reciting the *Vadonnaya* mantra, mixed with various fragrant substances.
Then, one should offer oblations to Aghora in the midst of the well-kindled fire;
having formed the *hetu-mudrā* and rendered [the victim] as if dead, one should perform the homa unobserved.
Having performed [the rites] in this manner during the night, one should then partake of the remnants of the sacrifice;
indeed, as soon as that has been consumed, one will come to be gazed upon by Cirañjīvin.
Immediately, honey-sweet accomplishment is placed in the hand, bestowing enjoyment;
the divine state arises, and the lord of practitioners becomes equal to Indra among mortals.

O Maheśvara, because he acts for the pleasure of the gods, there is no fault in the destruction of the world-cycle for practitioners who possess knowledge of the Kula, provided that liberation has been granted to them.
For the sake of causing this fruit to fall— fruit that is present at every step in the form of sin— he creates obstacles everywhere due to his own inherent contraction.
Likewise, he certainly creates obstacles for fruit-bearing trees;
yet, if by some stroke of fate, the loss of a fruit tree should ever occur, [he does not suffer].
O God, the practitioner should likewise be so; there is no doubt in this matter.
Whether by speech, or by mind, or even by body, if one is afflicted—
O Lord, if the fruit-bearing tree, which is the deity and the destroyer of Smara, or the family tree of the practitioner is harmed for his sake, then that deity perishes.
The worship of one's own family does not take place as long as there is no formal dismissal;
until then, conversation with those of one's own family must be avoided with great effort.
Indeed, there is no one on this earth capable of performing this task;
he must reside in a very remote region, devoid even of a name or caste.
If one performs [the rite], it may bring about either auspiciousness or an obstacle to the attainment of the fruit;
there is no fault in that, for practitioners and the family deities are not harmed.
But this, which is primarily characterized by obstacles, may sometimes be a means to achieve a result;
it becomes fruitful provided that even a common person acts upon it once the opportunity has been attained.
O Goddess of the gods, the fruit [of this] arises; one is certainly bound by sin.
There, blame accompanied by sweetness is born; of this there is no doubt.
O Lord, listen as I describe the fruit of Madhumatī:
a stream of nectar arises within the mouth.
The omniscient one, the sovereign of all scriptures, the leader of the family;
for as long as the moon and sun endure, he shall possess abundant prosperity and happiness.
With celestial maidens and apsarases, and with divine gandharvas and cāraṇas—
those who bring delight for the sake of nectar and are exceedingly rare objects of enjoyment for the gods.
O Supreme Lord, a celestial maiden, full of longing and with her heart yearning for the practitioner, arrives having mounted a chariot held by her hand.
Where the god Kāmeśvara has fallen under the power of anxiety,
there indeed the celestial maidens constantly go by the thousands.
Having made the city of Indrayogya, he rejoices together with practitioners;
thereafter, having attained liberation from that, he indeed enjoys manifold happiness in liberation.
Having remained on earth for a long time, one shall attain liberation at the end;
thus, O Lord, has this divine state that brings happiness been described to you.
O Mahādeva, O Guru Bhairava, the state of a hero (vīrabhāva) is not to be kept secret with effort from just any deity, but rather from a sacrificial animal.
Having become free from dualities in mind, with the form of the digit of desire (kāmakalā) in the heart,
one should indeed always be intent upon the supreme worship during the nights.
Taking his own family with him, he himself assumes the form of Bhairava;
the family assumes the form of Bhairavī, and the detailed ritual placement (nyāsa) is performed upon her limbs.
Having performed the entire ritual placement (nyāsa), including that consisting of the nine triangles,
[he should sit] upon a cushion of flowers in the midst of a profusion of blossoms.
Having written the yantra upon a family-owned object strewn with various fragrances,
one should worship the conch after first performing the ritual installation of the water-pot (ghaṭasthāpana).
Having drawn a hexagon on one's own left side with the aperture of Brahma (brahmarandhra) in its center,
one should indeed place there a pitcher made of gold or silver.
O Lord, one should place a water-pot (kumbha), fragrant with perfumes, made of copper, or of earth, or even one devoid of iron, according to the prescribed measure.
One should worship the Brahmins and others as the causal substance (*hetu-dravya*), distinguishing them according to their respective lineages;
having first inscribed the mantra therein, one should [worship] whichever family they have originated from.
There, one should meditate upon the supreme deity and recite [the mantra] one hundred and eight times;
then, displaying the *dhenumudrā*, one should contemplate that [water] as nectar (*amṛta*).
Upon seeing the vessel of the arghya offering, all the gods became eager;
all the Bhairavas danced, and the Mothers and the Gaṇas danced as well.
All the gods, beginning with Indra, dance, greedy for the honey;
Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Maheśa, and the others dance, intent on joy.
Having divided the vessel for the *argha* offering into two parts, one part is given to the Guru;
having thus bestowed it upon the lineage-elders (*kulāpada*), the propitiation of the deity is performed with the remaining one.
O God, having drunk the *kula-rasa* and being adorned with various ornaments,
if the Guru is not personally present, then one should discharge it into water.

Having become one whose very form is bliss, one should worship the Supreme Goddess after performing worship in the respective yantras according to the procedures prescribed in their respective Kalpas.
Then, having performed the rite of dismissal (visarjana), one should subsequently unite [the deity] with one's own lineage.
By drinking that nectar of the universe, I partake of immortality.
Through the tasting of the flavors at its corners, one attains the state of *sasaja*;
by the mere grasping of its fruit, there is the ascent to the peak of Mount Sumeru.
Merely by means of the *latā-liṅga*, her body becomes washed with nectar;
when the root-yoga (*mūlayoga*) has been performed there, one should recite [the mantra] eight thousand times.
Then, having taken the sacrificial substance purified by recitation, one should perform the libation;
O Lord, having performed the libation, one should follow while circumambulating.
Having prostrated and praised him with the hymn prescribed for the ritual manual, he should then offer water, saying:
"O Lord, this Vīrakula is beautiful and most enchanting."
O Bhairava, in whatever region that hero resides, or even his family,
there shall be no fear from forest-dwellers, nor any fear of kings and the like.
There shall always be great auspiciousness, increasing wealth and sons; there, O Mahādeva, may prosperity remain forever firm.
The mantra for awakening from dreams must certainly be applied with effort at the foot of a tree, and then no obstacle shall arise.
It cannot be seized by another hero even through divine means because of its connection [to that power],
nor is it joined with sins when it is united with the Yoginīs.
If one goes to a cremation ground on any Tuesday whatsoever,
there the fruit of worship shall be obtained for a duration of seven days.
If one departs on the fourteenth day, one obtains the fruit of the fortnightly worship;
but if one does not arrive and the sacred place remains unworshipped, there is no doubt that he is merely a beast.
"O God, there is no one superior to another"— for the practitioner who is thus intent on such thought, even if he should fall into agitation, no agitation whatsoever arises.
Through his initial effort, that best of heroes becomes possessed of enjoyment and happy;
through enjoyment he attains liberation, and through enjoyment he accomplishes the Kula practice.
O Maheśvara, without having attained the cause and being possessed of agitation,
one should not perform my worship, nor meditation, nor contemplation.
Therefore, having eaten and drunk, one should worship the Supreme Lord;
there is no fault in the splendor of the Krama, nor is there any corruption of conduct.
Whatever one speaks, sleeps, does, or acquires—all that should be performed while meditating upon it as having the form of the Kula; thus one shall dwell in happiness.
Alone, in a secluded place— whether in a cremation ground, on a mountain, in a forest,
in an empty house, or on a riverbank— he should always dwell free from attachment.
For heroes, the practice of recitation is praised at all times;
it should be performed in every land and at every sacred seat, without any doubt.
If a Brahmin should become fallen and devoted to the wealth of his lineage,
then he must perform the propitiation of the lineage according to this prescribed method.
Within the interior of the Aparā-flower, however, is the captivating seat of the Kula;
there is the face of all the gods, consisting of the essence of the arts of great desire.
O Lord Sadāśiva, you yourself are present as the flower that is the enemy of horses (the *hayāri*);
within that, one should take the sandalwood paste in the midst of the flowers.
Having offered blood, whether mixed or unmixed, which is of the nature of Śiva,
one should unite it with the power of Śiva (Śakti), contemplating their oneness with the intellect.

Having worshipped for a moment right there and made her resolve, the Supreme Goddess recited that very mantra over the substance situated within the sacrificial pit, which is most difficult to obtain.
O Bhairava, this substance, in which Aparājitā flowers and Javā flowers are present, should be known as superior to nectar and is very difficult to obtain.
Where there are red oleanders or white jasmine, or where a *droṇa* tree stands, the Goddess dwells there eternally; at its base is my place of worship.
If one offers even a single flower, one shall obtain silk cloth and fruit;
it is certain that sins such as the killing of a Brahmin perish in an instant.
But there is another, O Maheśvara, whose majesty indeed cannot be described;
however, O Hero, it must be performed by heroic men in the practice of *vīrasādhana*.
It should be performed even with divine beings, but not with beasts or outcasts;
it is better to perform it with an outcast than with a beast—this is the settled conclusion.
Whatever method for the accomplishment of mantras was previously taught by Śakti,
the heroic and exceedingly powerful one should perform it, including the preparation of collyrium, pills, and so forth.
The division of the divine [hero] by means of a hero, and that division of the woman, is now described:
it is sweet, full of goodness, and established in the grace of artistic skill.
A divine hero, however, is generally like a god, with his mind directed toward the higher realms;
he may be adorned with celestial ornaments or anointed with sandalwood paste.
Whether he conceals his true form or is manifest as Kulabhairava,
whether he is smeared with red sandalwood paste, or whether he is a Vaiṣṇava or even a non-Vaiṣṇava.
Whether conditioned or unconditioned, O Lord of the Family, you are eternally joined [to reality];
whether in contempt or in worship, may you always be joyful and well-nourished.
Whether they are intent on reviling the gods or intent on worshipping them, whether they are devoted to worship or devoid of it— those who abide by the path of the Kulīnas [are liberated].
Endowed with his own true nature, he shall roam upon the earth like a god;
the preliminary practice (puraścaryā) should be performed until the end of his lineage, and at night otherwise.
O Lord, just as there is no Vedic refinement for a twice-born man devoid of the Vedas,
so too devotion does not arise for one who is devoid of devotion to Viṣṇu.
Just as liberation without the knowledge of Śakti is considered a cause for laughter,
so too in the Tantra there is no entitlement whatsoever without a Guru.
Just as a woman who is husbandless is deprived of all ritual duties,
so too is a deity without a lineage, or a hero who is my practitioner.
O follower of the Kaula path, one who is not devoted to the inner state has no authority;
how can he whose family is undisciplined be a worshiper of me?
Therefore, one should act with such effort that it is endowed with discipline;
for in this scripture of the Kula, there is no authority whatsoever regarding existence or non-existence.
By that, the practitioner whose being is purified becomes a Kaulika.
The Illustrious Goddess said:
I shall explain the state of the sacrificial animal; listen with a concentrated mind, my child, regarding the offering of the animal according to the prescribed rule.
